stories.title: BlackRock: AI's role in driving crypto demand is 'underappreciated'
stories.summary: BlackRock says the market underappreciates AI as a driver of crypto demand, according to Cointelegraph. The comment links growth in AI infrastructure to future digital-asset demand. The report gives no data or mechanism behind the claim.
stories.whyItMatters: BlackRock runs the largest bitcoin ETF, so its public framing of demand drivers can shape institutional narratives and flows.
whatToWatch: Whether BlackRock follows up with data or research to support the claim
Similar commentary from other large asset managers
questions: What specific AI-to-crypto demand link is BlackRock describing?
Is this analysis or a pitch for BlackRock's own products?

sources.title: AI potential to drive crypto demand remains ‘underappreciated’: BlackRock

stories.title: Does Satoshi Nakamoto really hold 1.1 million Bitcoin?
stories.summary: A Cointelegraph feature revisits the long-standing claim that Bitcoin's creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, holds about 1.1 million BTC in dormant early wallets. The piece re-examines the on-chain evidence behind that widely cited number. No new coin movement was reported.
stories.whyItMatters: This dormant stash is one of the largest concentrated bitcoin holdings, so any change in its status could affect supply and sentiment.
whatToWatch: Any on-chain activity in wallets linked to Satoshi
New analysis that challenges or supports the 1.1 million BTC estimate
questions: How solid is the on-chain attribution behind this figure?
Would confirmed movement of these coins move the market?

sources.title: Big Questions: Does Satoshi actually own 1.1 million Bitcoin?

stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly to brief UN Security Council on AI risks
stories.summary: Reports cited by Cointelegraph say OpenAI and Anthropic will brief the UN Security Council on AI risks. No date or scope for the briefing was given. This story touches AI policy more than crypto markets directly.
stories.whyItMatters: AI policy shifts can affect sentiment around AI-linked crypto tokens and infrastructure, though the briefing itself is not a crypto event.
whatToWatch: Confirmation of the briefing date
Any public summary of what was presented
questions: What specific risks will the companies present?
Could this lead to concrete AI policy proposals?

sources.title: OpenAI, Anthropic to brief UN Security Council on AI risks: Reports

stories.title: Circle pays big for Binance distribution as stablecoin margins shrink
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, pays large distribution fees to Binance while its own margins come under pressure. The report frames this as a squeeze between rising distribution costs and shrinking stablecoin economics.
stories.whyItMatters: Circle issues one of the largest dollar stablecoins, so its margin pressure affects economics underpinning a large share of crypto trading and settlement.
whatToWatch: Circle's disclosed financials on stablecoin issuance margins
Whether other exchanges negotiate similar distribution fees
questions: How much of Circle's reserve income goes to distribution partners?
Can this arrangement last as stablecoin competition grows?

sources.title: Circle pays millions for Binance distribution while its margins collapse

stories.title: Coinbase details its post-quantum plan for Bitcoin custody
stories.summary: Decrypt reports on Coinbase's plan to protect the roughly $250 billion in bitcoin it custodies from future quantum-computing threats. The report outlines the exchange's early planning for quantum-resistant custody methods. Few technical specifics were given.
stories.whyItMatters: Quantum computing is a long-term but real risk to Bitcoin's cryptography, and custodians holding large client balances face pressure to plan ahead.
whatToWatch: Concrete timelines or standards Coinbase adopts
Whether other major custodians publish similar plans
questions: How soon could a real quantum threat to Bitcoin emerge?
Would a fix require a change to the Bitcoin protocol itself?

sources.title: Inside Coinbase’s $250 Billion Playbook for Post-Quantum Bitcoin Custody

stories.title: Rogue iPhone app broke out of iOS sandbox to steal $580,000 in USDT
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a malicious iPhone app escaped Apple's iOS sandbox protections. Attackers used the app to hijack $580,000 in USDT from victims. The failure sits at the mobile-security level, not the blockchain level.
stories.whyItMatters: Mobile-device compromise remains a major way crypto holders lose funds, and a sandbox escape points to a deeper gap in iOS security.
whatToWatch: Apple's response and any patch for the sandbox escape
Whether the app is identified and pulled from distribution
questions: How did the app pass review, if it went through the App Store?
Are other users still exposed to the same flaw?

sources.title: Rogue iPhone app escapes iOS sandbox to hijack $580,000 in USDT

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs absorb 11,500 BTC in biggest buying day in nearly two years
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in a net 11,500 BTC in one day, per CryptoSlate. That is the largest single-day accumulation in almost two years. The surge points to a pickup in institutional demand through the ETF wrapper.
stories.whyItMatters: Large ETF inflows give a concrete, trackable read on institutional demand and can affect the bitcoin supply available on exchanges.
whatToWatch: Whether the inflow pace holds in coming trading days
Which ETF issuers drove most of the buying
questions: Is this new institutional allocation or short-term repositioning?
How does it compare with outflows elsewhere in the market?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs just absorbed 11,500 BTC in their biggest buying day in nearly two years

stories.title: $161 million in decade-old Bitcoin has moved in two weeks
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that bitcoin wallets dormant for about a decade, holding a combined $161 million, became active and moved funds over a two-week span. The report does not name the wallet owners or their reasons for moving the coins.
stories.whyItMatters: Movement of long-dormant whale coins is closely watched as a possible sign of early-holder selling, though the motive is often unclear.
whatToWatch: Whether the moved coins reach exchanges, which would suggest a sale
Any on-chain analysis that identifies the wallets' owners
questions: Are these coordinated moves or separate, unrelated wallets?
Does the destination of the funds point to a sale or just custody changes?

sources.title: $161 Million in Decade-Old Bitcoin Has Moved in Just Two Weeks

stories.title: CME adds Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures to its crypto lineup
stories.summary: CME Group is expanding its regulated crypto futures products to include Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap contracts, per Decrypt. This adds to CME's existing bitcoin and ether futures. The report gives no launch date.
stories.whyItMatters: Regulated futures listings widen institutional access to hedging and exposure for more tokens, marking a step toward mainstream market infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Launch date and early trading volume for the new contracts
Whether CME adds more altcoin futures after this
questions: Will demand for these contracts match CME's existing crypto products?
Could listing on CME affect spot liquidity for these tokens?

sources.title: CME Expands Crypto Futures Lineup With Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap

stories.title: Bitcoin's path to quantum safety may leave Lightning privacy exposed
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Bitcoin's base layer may be able to move toward quantum-resistant cryptography. But privacy gaps on the Lightning Network could remain even after such an upgrade. The report treats quantum safety and Lightning privacy as separate, unresolved issues.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a real tradeoff for developers: a quantum-safe Bitcoin base layer would not automatically fix second-layer privacy weaknesses.
whatToWatch: Developer proposals that address Lightning privacy alongside quantum-resistance work
Progress on any quantum-safe signature scheme for Bitcoin
questions: What specific privacy gap does Lightning keep under a quantum-safe upgrade?
How far off is real quantum-resistance work for Bitcoin?

sources.title: Bitcoin may go quantum-safe while Lightning privacy stays exposed

stories.title: Zcash gets its first European ETP after its US ETF launch
stories.summary: Zcash has received its first exchange-traded product listing in Europe, following a recent US ETF launch for the privacy-focused cryptocurrency, per Cointelegraph. The report does not name the issuer of the new European product.
stories.whyItMatters: A new regulated wrapper for a privacy coin gives mainstream investors easier access to an asset class regulators often treat warily.
whatToWatch: Trading volume and inflows into the new European ETP
Whether other privacy coins get similar ETP or ETF listings
questions: Will European regulators treat a privacy-coin ETP differently than a bitcoin one?
Is investor demand strong enough to justify more privacy-coin products?

sources.title: Zcash gets first European ETP following US ETF launch

stories.title: Arch Lending eyes tokenized stocks as its next collateral market
stories.summary: Arch Lending is exploring tokenized stocks as a new form of loan collateral, per Cointelegraph. The move would extend crypto-native lending to include tokenized versions of traditional equities. The report gives no launch timeline.
stories.whyItMatters: Using tokenized stocks as loan collateral would be a concrete step in merging crypto lending markets with traditional equity exposure.
whatToWatch: Which tokenized stock products Arch Lending integrates first
How regulators react to tokenized-equity collateral arrangements
questions: What custody and liquidation rules would apply to this collateral?
Which jurisdictions would allow this kind of lending product?

sources.title: Arch Lending eyes tokenized stocks as next collateral market
